\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{শ্রদ্ধা} \bn{করা} (shrôddhā kôrā)}{শ্রদ্ধা করা (shrôddhā kôrā)}]{\bn{শ্রদ্ধা} \bn{করা} (shrôddhā kôrā) — to respect deeply; to revere}

\label{lesson:BN-C351-shroddha-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for truthful, then the Bengali for fair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{শ্রদ্ধা} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{শ্রদ্ধা} \bn{করা}} — \emph{shrôddhā kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to respect deeply; to revere\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{গ্রামের} \bn{সবাই} \bn{ডাক্তারকে} \bn{শ্রদ্ধা} \bn{করে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{grāmer sôbāi ḍāktārke shrôddhā kôre.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone in the village looks up to the doctor.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{সবাইকে} \bn{শ্রদ্ধা} \bn{করতেন}, \emph{tini sôbāike shrôddhā kôrten}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{শ্রদ্ধা} \bn{করা}} (\emph{shrôddhā kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{śraddhā}, faith or trust (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}. It is deeper than \bn{সম্মান}: the respect you feel for a teacher or an elder.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shrôddhā kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shrôddhā kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grāmer sôbāi ḍāktārke shrôddhā kôre.} — Everyone in the village looks up to the doctor.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for truthful, then the Bengali for fair, then say \emph{shrôddhā kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{শ্রদ্ধা} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To respect deeply; to revere\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অবহেলা} \bn{করা} (ôbôhelā kôrā)}{অবহেলা করা (ôbôhelā kôrā)}]{\bn{অবহেলা} \bn{করা} (ôbôhelā kôrā) — to neglect}

\label{lesson:BN-C351-obohela-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for fair, then the Bengali for to revere.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অবহেলা} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{অবহেলা} \bn{করা}} — \emph{ôbôhelā kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to neglect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{তুমি} \bn{তোমার} \bn{স্বাস্থ্য} \bn{অবহেলা} \bn{করছ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tumi tomār svāsthyô ôbôhelā kôrchhô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
You are neglecting your health.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{কাজটা} \bn{অবহেলা} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini kājṭā ôbôhelā kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অবহেলা} \bn{করা}} (\emph{ôbôhelā kôrā}) is Sanskrit \emph{avahelā}, beside \emph{avahelana}, disrespect (Monier-Williams), with \bn{করা}: to treat a thing as not worth care.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbôhelā kôrā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbôhelā kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tumi tomār svāsthyô ôbôhelā kôrchhô.} — You are neglecting your health.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for fair, then the Bengali for to revere, then say \emph{ôbôhelā kôrā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অবহেলা} \bn{করা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To neglect\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অবজ্ঞা} (ôbôgyā)}{অবজ্ঞা (ôbôgyā)}]{\bn{অবজ্ঞা} (ôbôgyā) — disdain; contempt}

\label{lesson:BN-C351-obogya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to revere, then the Bengali for to neglect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অবজ্ঞা}}
\textbf{\bn{অবজ্ঞা}} — \emph{ôbôgyā} — \textquotedblleft{}disdain; contempt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{গরিব} \bn{মানুষকে} \bn{অবজ্ঞা} \bn{করা} \bn{অন্যায়।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gôrib mānushke ôbôgyā kôrā ônyāy.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
It is wrong to look down on poor people.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অবজ্ঞা}} (\emph{ôbôgyā}) is Sanskrit \emph{avajñā}, \emph{ava-} 'down' with \emph{jñā} 'knowing': to think little of (Monier-Williams). \bn{জ্ঞ} is said gy, as in \bn{জ্ঞান}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbôgyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôbôgyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gôrib mānushke ôbôgyā kôrā ônyāy.} — It is wrong to look down on poor people.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to revere, then the Bengali for to neglect, then say \emph{ôbôgyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অবজ্ঞা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Disdain; contempt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{কদর} (kôdôr)}{কদর (kôdôr)}]{\bn{কদর} (kôdôr) — esteem; appreciation}

\label{lesson:BN-C351-kodor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to neglect, then the Bengali for disdain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{কদর}}
\textbf{\bn{কদর}} — \emph{kôdôr} — \textquotedblleft{}esteem; appreciation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{দেশে} \bn{শিল্পীদের} \bn{কদর} \bn{নেই।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ei deshe shilpīder kôdôr nei.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Artists are not valued in this country.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{কদর}} (\emph{kôdôr}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{qadr}, worth, through Persian: the worth others see in you.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôdôr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kôdôr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ei deshe shilpīder kôdôr nei.} — Artists are not valued in this country.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to neglect, then the Bengali for disdain, then say \emph{kôdôr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{কদর} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Esteem; appreciation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{খাতির} \bn{করা} (khātir kôrā)}{খাতির করা (khātir kôrā)}]{\bn{খাতির} \bn{করা} (khātir kôrā) — to treat with regard; to make much of (someone)}

\label{lesson:BN-C351-khatir-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for disdain, then the Bengali for esteem.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{খাতির} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{খাতির} \bn{করা}} — \emph{khātir kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to treat with regard; to make much of (someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{গ্রামের} \bn{লোকেরা} \bn{অতিথিদের} \bn{খাতির} \bn{করে।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{grāmer lokerā ôtithider khātir kôre.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The villagers make a fuss of their guests.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{আমাদের} \bn{খাতির} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini āmāder khātir kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{খাতির} \bn{করা}} (\emph{khātir kôrā}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{khāṭir}, the mind and so regard for someone, through Persian, with \bn{করা}: to treat a guest or an elder with warm attention.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khātir kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{grāmer lokerā ôtithider khātir kôre.} — The villagers make a fuss of their guests.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for disdain, then the Bengali for esteem, then say \emph{khātir kôrā} again
\end{itemize}
